title: HarborCare 14 Procurement: MSA/DPA, SLAs, Pricing, Onboarding
summary: Procurement kickoff to review Redwood MSA/DPA redlines, SLA options for Dedicated vs Hosted, initial pricing for 3-6 month pilot, and onboarding timeline. Customer requested SOC2, network diagrams, and a pricing sheet with committed capacity options. Agreed next steps: send redlined MSA/DPA, pricing & SLA sheet, schedule technical kick-off week of 5/11-5/15.
topics: Pricing for pilot and committed capacity discounts
Security artifacts: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-07 15:00 PT — Duration 55m — Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Olivia (HarborCare Procurement), Marcus (HarborCare Legal), Priya (CTO), Evan (Infra)

[00:00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — um — appreciate you making time. I see we have the procurement and legal folks on — quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Olivia: Olivia here (Procurement).
[00:00:08] Marcus: Marcus, Legal.
[00:00:10] Priya: Priya, CTO. Evan on infra coming in a bit.
[00:00:15] Samir: Great. Maya and Jordan from our side, thanks. Today objective is to walk through the MSA/DPA redlines you sent, cover SLAs and pricing options for the pilot, and run through onboarding — any specific must-haves up front?
[00:00:32] Olivia: Yeah, main things: data residency for PII, retention limits, audit logs, and explicit KMS/HSM language. Also we need to understand how Dedicated vs Hosted changes our exposure and liability.
[00:00:45] Marcus: From legal, we have a couple of standard redlines on indemnity and data breach notification timeframes — 48 hours is our ask — we saw Redwood's standard 72 hour.
[00:00:58] Maya: Okay, noted. We can, um, go through each redline. On the breach notification window, we typically commit to 72 hours in our hosted plan — for Dedicated and Private we can usually move closer to 48 with contractual SLAs and escalations.
[00:01:14] Priya: Can you clarify Dedicated here? We heard Dedicated gives predictable throughput but is the control plane still managed by Redwood? We have strict network segmentation rules.
[00:01:25] Jordan: Good question. For Redwood Dedicated, the serving runtime is in a customer-dedicated GPU pool — infra is logically isolated. The control plane remains managed by us but we support VPC peering and private endpoints; for full private deployment (Redwood Private), the control plane can be customer-controlled in a VPC or on-prem. Sometimes our docs say "private control plane" — apologies if name confuses.
[00:01:51] Priya: Right, that's what I wanted to confirm — we likely need Redwood Private for HIPAA-sensitive workloads.
[00:01:58] Samir: Understood. For pilot we usually start with Hosted or Dedicated; moving to Redwood Private is a larger ask but doable — requires additional engagement and an enterprise contract.
[00:02:09] Evan: Quick question on logging — do you provide immutable audit logs and do they integrate with Splunk/Datadog?
[00:02:15] Maya: We push audit logs to your S3 or customer log collector. Integration with Splunk/Datadog is supported; format is JSON with request IDs. Note sometimes auto-transcription of docs show K-V cache as K V cache — ok sorry aside — the logs include model routing and tenant IDs.
[00:02:33] Marcus: About the DPA — we flagged sub-processor list and asked for 30 day notice for new sub-processors. Is that acceptable?
[00:02:42] Samir: Standard is 30 days for major changes; we can commit to notification and an option to object for a period; for certain cloud infra changes we may be limited by provider windows.
[00:02:53] Olivia: On SLA credits — we need 99.95% uptime for production endpoints and a clear service credit schedule. Your pricing team proposed a 99.9% for hosted. Can you bridge that?
[00:03:06] Maya: So 99.95% is available on Dedicated with SLA add-on; hosted tier's standard is 99.9. There are also multi-region routing options to help meet the 99.95 — but that implies egress and cross-region charges and slightly different failover behavior.
[00:03:24] Priya: How much more would Dedicated cost for our expected 500k tokens/month pilot?
[00:03:29] Samir: We'll share the pricing sheet — rough ballpark: hosted is pay-as-you-go, Dedicated reserved pool with monthly commit gives ~30-40% cost reduction at scale but requires a month-to-month reservation. For the pilot we can do a small committed Dedicated node set; I'll follow up with precise numbers.
[00:03:44] Olivia: Please include unit economics and breakout for token costs vs embedding calls — procurement needs line items.
[00:03:50] Samir: Absolutely.
[00:03:52] Marcus: A few legal items: indemnity cap, data breach notification as we said, and audit right window — we prefer rolling 12 months for audit logs retention.
[00:04:03] Jordan: On audit rights we can grant SOC 2 reports and allow for vendor audits under certain redacted scopes; full on-site audits are possible under private contracts but have logistic constraints.
[00:04:18] Olivia: Can you send your SOC2 report and network diagrams?
[00:04:21] Maya: Yes — I'll attach SOC 2 Type II, our latest pen-test summary, and a network diagram. Expect those in next email.
[00:04:29] Evan: For onboarding — what does the technical kick-off look like? Sequence: credentials, test keys, run perf baseline, then ramp?
[00:04:36] Maya: Typical: 1) Send tenant and API keys to staging, 2) run basic smoke and perf scripts (we'll provide runbook), 3) tune batching/quantization recommendations, 4) go to pilot with monitoring hooks in Redwood Console. We usually allocate SE hours for the first two weeks.
[00:04:55] Priya: Is there a recommended quantization profile? We're on A100s in our infra.
[00:05:00] Maya: For A100s we recommend 4-bit quantization for cost savings while preserving quality; we'll include model-specific profiles.
[00:05:06] Samir: Ok let's move to redlines — Olivia or Marcus you had specific doc references?
[00:05:12] Marcus: I'll call out section 7 indemnity and section 11 breach. Also data retention in DPA — we want 90 day default, with options for longer retention on request.
[00:05:23] Samir: We can accept 90 day default and add clause for extended retention as an addendum. For indemnity cap we typically propose a cap equal to fees paid in prior 12 months; open to discussion.
[00:05:36] Marcus: That's a starting point; legal will propose language.
[00:05:39] Olivia: Procurement timeline — we need final pricing and any PO flow to approve by 5/21 to meet our internal launch window.
[00:05:46] Samir: Noted. We'll aim to get the redlined MSA/DPA and pricing sheet sent by 5/10.
[00:05:50] Jordan: Also FYI we can offer a pilot discount for early-stage pilots and will outline SE hours included.
[00:05:58] Priya: For the pilot we want a perf benchmark — 99th percentile latency target under 1s for short-chat prompts. Can you commit to running baseline tests?
[00:06:08] Maya: Yes — SE will run a perf baseline against our runtime and provide per-route latency breakdown in Redwood Console. For very low 99th p99 <1s we recommend smaller context windows and model selection; we'll document trade-offs.
[00:06:23] Evan: Any concerns about data egress when using Dedicated across regions?
[00:06:28] Maya: There are egress costs and potential latency increase; we'll include regional routing policy recommendations and cost estimates in the pricing sheet.
[00:06:36] Olivia: Ok, quick recap and next steps?
[00:06:40] Samir: Recap: Samir/Maya to send: 1) redlined MSA/DPA template with proposed counter language, 2) SOC2 and security artifacts, 3) pricing sheet with hosted vs Dedicated vs Redwood Private options and SLA tiers, 4) onboarding runbook and proposed dates for tech kick-off. HarborCare to send redlines and any non-negotiable clauses, and confirm pilot capacity and PO timeline.
[00:07:05] Marcus: We'll try to provide legal redlines by 5/12.
[00:07:08] Olivia: Procurement will review pricing and aim to approve PO by 5/21 if numbers align.
[00:07:12] Samir: Great — Maya will schedule the kick-off for next week — we have availability 5/12 or 5/14 — which works best?
[00:07:21] Priya: 5/14 better for our infra folks.
[00:07:24] Jordan: I'll put calendar invite for 5/14 10am PT.
[00:07:27] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in an email with the artifacts.

[00:07:40] [END]
